messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1: High error rate and container crashes in serving cluster prod-us-east-1. Symptoms: CUDA OOMs, container restarts, and RDMA link flaps detected. Triggered by elevated token throughput. Paging on-call.

alice: oncall here, looking now. seeing a spike in 503s and a lot of `cudaOutOfMemory` in the logs for model-serving pods.

samir: I can see RDMA errors too from the node exporters: `mlx5 0000:81:00.0: async event: link down` and packet drops on IB interface.

ingrid: copying stdout from one of the restarted containers: ```
2024-09-15T14:02:12Z ERROR generation_runner: cuda runtime error (2): out of memory at /workspace/runtime.cu:412
stack: ...
container restarted (OOMKilled)
```

joel: netops-bot shows multiple link flaps in rack r07, top-of-rack switch reports neighbor flaps for ports 11-14 (InfiniBand).

netops-bot: NetOps Alert: IB fabric reports 12% packet loss on subnet 2; flapping links detected between leaf-07 and spine-03. Suggested action: isolate affected nodes.

carla: tagging netops and infra. @netops please confirm if this is hardware or config. Can we fail traffic to another rack while investigating?

netops-bot: NetOps: we're seeing increased CRC errors on port 11/leaf-07. Likely physical layer or cable; RMA candidate if persists. Initiating fabric reroute for critical subnets in 60s.

alice: temporary mitigations: 1) reduce tokenizer batch_size for real-time routes to cut memory usage; 2) enable TCP fallback for serving pods that support it; 3) cordon and drain obviously broken nodes. Starting step 1 now.

samir: rolling a config change to reduce batch target from 64->16 on /v1/generate and canarying to 10% of traffic. Patch applied to route config: ```
route: /v1/generate
model_variant: redwood/llama-13b
batch_target: 16
```

ingrid: batch reduction helped memory errors on some pods, but we still see container restarts where RDMA is flapping. Those pods use multi-node KV cache pinned to IB.

joel: suggestion: for affected node pool (np-gpu-r07) switch to TCP-based ibverbs fallback (i.e., disable mlx5 RDMA) for serving processes, to keep them up while hardware is diagnosed. That avoids cross-node RDMA traffic.

carla: infra approval to modify kernel RDMA settings for those nodes? This is a P1.

oncall-2nd: I'm taking over the RDMA change window. Will push kernel param toggle via salt. Command to run on nodes: ```
sudo echo 1 > /sys/class/infiniband/mlx5_0/device/disable_hca
# or use ibdev2netdev to set dev down/up
```
Proceeding on nodes: gpu-r07-11, gpu-r07-12, gpu-r07-13.

alice: warning — disabling HCA will break any running multi-node allreduce jobs (training), but we have very few in prod serving. Proceed.

samir: running `kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-r07-11` before changes: several model-serving pods on that node had RESTARTS > 5 in last 10m and `OOMKilled`.

oncall-2nd: executed HCA disable on gpu-r07-11 and gpu-r07-12. Observed IB link state go DOWN and then routing moved to TCP. Serving pods now show fewer RDMA errors in logs.

alice: good. monitoring: customer-facing errors dropped from 18% -> 6% in the last 5m. Continuing.

ingrid: observed `nvidia-smi` on affected hosts: memory freed up on resumed pods, and `dmesg` shows fewer `mlx5` errors after disable. Pasting sample: ```
[  100.123456] mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: mlx5_core: unload HCA
[  100.124000] mlx5_core: IB device disabled by admin
```

joel: now need a plan: either (A) keep RDMA disabled on these nodes until hardware RMA + cabling check, or (B) move all serving traffic off this rack to other racks / region. Option A reduces perf slightly (TCP fallback), B could increase cross-rack cost. Thoughts?

carla: Ops preference: keep TCP fallback on for 2 hours while netops investigates and schedules cable swap. If netops confirms it's physical, we'll RMA. Inform customers if impacted beyond 2 hours.

netops-bot: NetOps update: tech on-site scheduled 45m. Initial inspection shows slightly loose QSFP on leaf-07 port 11; reseating momentarily reduced flaps but not permanently. Cabling replacement recommended.

samir: also noticed autoscaler started spawning extra pods to compensate but those pods hit the same RDMA flaps before we disabled HCA; scaled back to avoid oscillation. Patch: set autoscaler cooldown to 10m for this ASG.

alice: done. cooldown increased. Also toggled automatic fallback policy to prefer TCP for model variants that checkpoint KV over the network.

oncall-2nd: after HCA disable, observed 504s→503s→back to normal for some routes. Still tail latencies ~120ms (up from 60ms) on heavy generation routes. We're monitoring SLAs.

support-bot: Customer impact: 24 customers saw elevated error rates; top affected tenants: finco-prod, chatapp-eu. Support notified and sending post-incident updates if degradation persists >1h.

carla: please collect per-customer error counts and a short mitigation note for the postmortem. 

ingrid: grabbing logs and `kubectl describe pod` outputs for 10 sample pods and saving in incident artifacts. Example `kubectl describe` shows: ```
Events:
  Warning  OOMKilled  2m (x4 over 8m)  kubelet  Container killed due to OOM
  Normal   BackOff    1m (x12 over 6m)  kubelet  Back-off restarting failed container
```

samir: analysis so far: primary cause was RDMA link instability causing increased packet loss and timeouts for KV cache RPCs. That caused retries and higher memory pressure (bigger in-flight KV caches), leading to CUDA OOMs and container restarts. Disabling HCA removed RDMA path and forced TCP fallback which reduced packet loss impact at the cost of latency.

joel: long-term fixes to propose: 1) stronger fabric monitoring and automatic rack isolation, 2) fallback policy to switch to TCP earlier when packet loss >5%, 3) investigate more resilient KV caching with backpressure under network retries.

carla: agreed. Also add a runbook step: when mlx5 link flaps >X/minute, automatically cordon nodes and shift traffic.

netops-bot: NetOps: cable replacement done on leaf-07 ports 11-14. Initial tests show stable link states. Re-enable plan: we will re-enable HCA one node at a time during a maintenance window and validate error rates.

oncall-2nd: scheduling re-enable for next safe window (in 30m). Will re-enable gpu-r07-11 first. Procedure: 1) uncordon node 2) enable HCA via sysfs 3) watch for `mlx5` events and serving errors for 10m. Rollback if flaps.

alice: re-enable started on gpu-r07-11. `echo 0 > /sys/class/infiniband/mlx5_0/device/disable_hca`

ingrid: after re-enable, small flaps observed for ~90s then steady. Monitoring: no immediate return of packet loss. Customer error rate holding low.

samir: re-enabled on gpu-r07-12 and gpu-r07-13 as well. All good so far. NetOps says cables replaced and QSFPs re-seated; will keep observation window for 2 hours.

carla: marking incident as mitigated for now. We'll leave follow-up actions and the postmortem tasks in the incident tracker.

alice: handoff notes for next on-call: root cause was intermittent InfiniBand cable/hardware failures causing packet loss and timeouts. Immediate mitigations performed: reduced batch sizes, enabled TCP fallback, cordoned/drained problematic nodes, disabled HCA temporarily, adjusted autoscaler and cooldowns. Current status: fabric stable, re-enabled RDMA on repaired nodes.

oncall-2nd: taking over. I'll watch metrics for next 2 hours and coordinate with NetOps to confirm RMA if any further flaps. Adding action items to incident tracker: RMA QSFPs, runbook update, implement automated fallback threshold.

support-bot: Notified affected customers with interim summary and ETA for post-incident report.

carla: thanks team. closing the active paging loop. Please file postmortem and include logs/artifacts.

alice: filing postmortem now, will include timeline, command snippets, and mitigations.

samir: leaving a quick checklist in the incident thread: ```
- [ ] Postmortem doc + timeline
- [ ] RMA schedule + ticket
- [ ] Runbook update for RDMA flaps
- [ ] Telemetry rule: if IB packet loss > 5% alert and auto-failover
- [ ] Perf regression analysis after TCP fallback
```

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. If errors rise above threshold, auto-escalate.
